extracted.intended_audience: accrediting entities, adoption service providers (ASPs), primary providers, approved persons, and other stakeholders involved in U.S. intercountry adoption accreditation and approval
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and criteria in 22 CFR Part 96 governing accreditation of agencies and approval of persons to provide intercountry adoption services, including standards for providers, accrediting entities, recordkeeping, reporting, adverse actions, and special procedures for relative adoptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption service definitions (22 CFR 96.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption service means any one of the following six services: (1) Identifying a child for adoption and arranging an adoption; (2) Securing the necessary consent to termination of parental rights and to adoption; (3) Performing a background study on a child or a home study on a prospective adoptive parent(s), and reporting on such a study; (4) Making non-judicial determinations of the best interests of a child and the appropriateness of an adoptive placement for the child; (5) Monitoring a case after a child has been placed with prospective adoptive parent(s) until final adoption; or (6) When necessary because of a disruption before final adoption, assuming custody and providing (including facilitating the provision of) child care or any other social service pending an alternative placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These six discrete services define the scope of adoption services for purposes of service plans, alternative procedures (e.g., for relative adoptions), and regulatory obligations. The rule references these service numbers throughout (e.g., §96.100 uses services 3, 5, and 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative procedures for primary providers in intercountry adoption by relatives (§96.100)
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where a child is being adopted by a relative (as defined in §96.2), the primary provider develops and implements a service plan addressing adoption service 3 (home/background studies), adoption service 5 (post-placement monitoring until final adoption), and adoption service 6 (assuming custody/providing child care or other social services if disruption occurs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary providers include any additional adoption services in the plan only if they or their supervised providers will actually provide them; must verify prospective adoptive parents have met training requirements in §96.48 before finalization or granting legal custody; all services must be performed in accordance with the Convention, the IAA, the UAA, and implementing regulations. Effective date January 8, 2025. Appendix A compares definitions of 'relative' in 8 CFR and 22 CFR for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: State licensing and compliance with all applicable laws (§96.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and persons must be licensed and operate in compliance with all applicable laws, including foreign-country laws where they provide adoption services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule retains standards requiring compliance with the Convention, the IAA, the UAA, and foreign and State laws; the Department declined to create a duplicative §96.29 and instead kept these principles in §96.30 (State Licensing and Compliance With All Applicable Laws).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on child buying and inducement; payments and recordkeeping (§96.36 and §96.36(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits child buying and inducement; recognizes permitted or required payments for specific child welfare activities when allowed by the child's country of origin but reinforces prohibitions on payments that are remitted as payment or inducement to release a child for adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department did not adopt a categorical prohibition on payments for child care; instead it augmented recordkeeping requirements (§96.36(b)) to increase oversight of permitted or required payments, to help ensure funds intended for children are not diverted to illicit purposes. Payments must be documented; enhanced recordkeeping assists oversight of payments by employees and supervised providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee policies and procedures (§96.40 and related provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and policies govern adoption fees and expenses, disclosure of fees to prospective adoptive parents, and how agencies structure and report fee schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department paused on revising §96.40 after commenters expressed concern that proposed changes did not reflect agency practice or flexibility needs. The rule retains attention to fee policies; accrediting entities now have a process for reporting fee schedule changes (see changes to §96.8). Commenters emphasized burden on ASPs to revise, recalculate, and report fee schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and post-placement monitoring until final adoption (§96.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards require ASPs to monitor placements and take action in the event of a disruption, and to report appropriately regarding disruption cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department received comments that proposed expansions of §96.50 would impose significant resource burdens; the final rule did not include those proposed revisions but retains monitoring and disruption-related standards as important services (including in relative adoptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement standards in outgoing convention cases (§96.54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing placement procedures, safeguards, and requirements for outgoing Convention adoption cases (children emigrating from the U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many commenters opposed proposed changes to §96.54 arguing negative impacts on outgoing adoption practice; the Department did not adopt the proposed revisions and left §96.54 unchanged in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using providers in foreign countries; payments to foreign supervised providers (§96.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for use and oversight of foreign supervised providers, including payment routing and disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department limited changes but added requirements (§96.46(b)(7) and (8)) that all payments to foreign supervised providers be provided through the primary provider and that the primary provider must give prospective adoptive parents a written explanation about the return of unused funds within 60 days. The Department signaled intent to consult further on broader oversight issues for foreign supervised providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and training of prospective adoptive parents in incoming cases (§96.48 and §96.38 additions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for parent preparation and training for incoming cases; primary providers must verify training requirements have been met before finalization or granting legal custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department did not increase hours as commenters requested but accepted adding training topics in §96.38 (e.g., trauma-informed parenting, impact on children already in the home, parental support for children who experience discrimination based on race, physical, cognitive, and other disabilities). In relative cases, primary providers must verify training compliance as soon as practicable if training occurred prior to provider involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing, compliance, and corporate governance (Subpart F overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards addressing licensing, compliance with applicable laws, and corporate governance of agencies and persons providing adoption services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart F groups multiple standards (licensing, governance, financial and risk management, ethical practices). The preamble emphasizes compliance with U.S. implementing statutes and foreign laws, and clarifies that the rule explains how providers should approach best-interests determinations when children are outside State jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal structure and oversight (§96.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing agencies' internal organizational structure and oversight mechanisms, including oversight of supervised providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department did not adopt a proposed requirement that agencies retain records related to monitoring and oversight of supervised providers for 25 years due to cost concerns; it retained existing language instead of extending retention to 25 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget, audit, insurance, and risk assessment requirements (§96.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial and risk-management standards for agencies and persons, including requirements relating to budgets, audits, insurance, and assessment of financial risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule retained existing wording in §96.33(e) (including references to 'financial resources' and cash reserves) rather than adopting proposed deletions or references to liquid assets; the Department avoided ambiguous new formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation standards (§96.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation paid to agency personnel must not be unreasonably high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department did not adopt the proposed vague 'actually cost' formulation; the final rule keeps a mandate against unreasonably high compensation but avoids an impractical standard for accrediting entities to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of agencies and persons to provide adoption services consistent with the Convention (§96.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards requiring agencies and persons to demonstrate suitability to provide adoption services in a manner consistent with the Hague Adoption Convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ethical/practice suitability standard referenced in Subpart F; accrediting entities are to evaluate applicants against Convention-consistent suitability criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and experience requirements for social service personnel (§96.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum education and experience qualifications required for social service staff providing adoption-related services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accrediting entities and agencies must ensure social service personnel meet these qualifications as part of accreditation and approval evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for social service personnel (§96.38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training standards for social service personnel, including required topics and competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department accepted adding topics such as trauma-informed parenting, impacts on children already in the home, and support for children experiencing discrimination; accrediting entities should ensure these training topics are included as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information disclosure and quality control practices (§96.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing what information must be disclosed to prospective adoptive parents and quality control policies and practices of agencies and persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule strengthens recordkeeping and disclosure practices to increase transparency and oversight; agencies must follow disclosure and quality control standards in client service agreements and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for responding to complaints and improving service delivery (§96.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint handling standards: how complaints are submitted, documented, and processed by accrediting entities and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 96.41 establishes that a complaint may be submitted by email, must include the name of the complainant and must be dated. Accrediting entities must maintain written records documenting each complaint and steps taken in response; procedures for disclosing information about substantiated complaints are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention, preservation, and disclosure of adoption records (§96.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for retention, preservation, and disclosure of adoption records held by agencies, persons, and accrediting entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule retained proposed changes requiring accrediting entities to retain records relating to accreditation decision-making for at least 10 years (§96.7 and §96.26). The Department declined to require 25-year retention for monitored provider oversight records due to cost concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case tracking, data management, and reporting (§96.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards requiring agencies and accrediting entities to track cases, manage data, and report specified information to the Secretary and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed reporting requirements are specified in §96.94 (annual and semi-annual reports) and §96.43; the Department rejected proposed expansion requiring extensive additional reporting of 'material facts' to foreign Central Authorities and the Secretary in §96.52(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Using supervised providers in the United States (§96.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards governing the use and oversight of supervised providers domiciled in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervised providers must be overseen by primary providers; the final rule clarified the term 'supervised provider' by adding 'domestic or' before 'foreign entity'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of home studies in incoming cases (§96.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and practical steps for performing and withdrawing home study recommendations in incoming cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule incorporates practical steps and timelines for withdrawal of a home study recommendation, including notifying adoptive parents, primary providers, and USCIS. §96.47 provides procedural guidance for withdrawal and communication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of medical and social information in incoming cases (§96.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards requiring provision of medical and social information about the child in incoming cases to prospective adoptive parents and relevant authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure accurate and timely medical/social information is provided as part of referral and placement processes, consistent with the Convention and implementing statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-adoption services in incoming cases (§96.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards requiring provision of post-adoption services, including monitoring and support after placement until final adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-adoption services are required in incoming cases; the Department emphasizes these services apply equally in adoptions by relatives and are essential to child well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance of communication and coordination functions in incoming cases (§96.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for ASPs' communication and coordination roles with foreign Central Authorities, USCIS, and other stakeholders in incoming cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department did not retain a proposed expansion requiring extensive additional reporting to the Secretary and foreign Central Authorities about 'material facts' of cases; however agencies must still perform required coordination and communication functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance of Convention communication and coordination functions on outgoing Convention cases (§96.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for performance of Convention communication and coordination duties in outgoing Convention adoption cases (U.S. child emigrating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must meet Convention obligations when communicating and coordinating on outgoing cases; the final rule did not adopt major proposed changes to §96.54 that commenters opposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation, performance criteria, authorities, and duties of accrediting entities (§96.4, §96.6, §96.7, §96.8, §96.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and procedures for selecting and designating accrediting entities, performance criteria for designation, authorities and responsibilities, fees charged by accrediting entities, and suspension or cancellation of designation by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable final-rule provisions include requiring accrediting entities to retain all records relating to accreditation decision-making for at least 10 years (§96.7), establishing a process for reporting accrediting entity fee schedule changes in the Federal Register (§96.8), and permitting Secretary findings that accrediting entities are out of compliance when the Secretary must intervene and impose adverse actions (§96.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to information and protection of documents requested by accrediting entity (§96.25 and §96.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards requiring applicants to provide information and documents to accrediting entities and standards for protecting such information and documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule requires retention of accurate records of accreditation and approval decision-making for at least 10 years (§96.26) and clarifies obligations to provide requested documentation to accrediting entities during evaluation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive criteria for evaluating applicants for accreditation or approval (§96.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive standards used by accrediting entities to evaluate applications for accreditation or approval, including taking into account reasons underlying previous denials (§96.27(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accrediting entities must consider prior denials and the reasons underlying those denials when evaluating new applications for accreditation or approval; §96.27 outlines the substantive criteria against which applicants are assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and requirements for adverse action by the Secretary (§96.83 and related sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules governing Secretary-imposed adverse actions (suspension, cancellation), including notification, standards for review, opportunities to request withdrawal of suspension/cancellation, and distinction from accrediting entity procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule introduces due-process-like features for Secretary adverse actions (e.g., §§96.84(a)-(b) for requests to withdraw suspension/cancellation), explains why some procedures may go farther than accrediting entity procedures because of emergent child-safety concerns, and provides mechanisms for petitions for relief (§96.84(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment procedures with prior notice (§96.88) and debarment effective immediately (§96.89)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed procedural requirements, time frames, notice contents, evidentiary standards, and review rights for debarment proceedings when the Secretary gives prior notice (§96.88) and when debarment is effective immediately due to risk of significant harm (§96.89).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule sets notice content requirements (reasons, standards alleged out of compliance, period/effect), timelines for written responses (30-day windows), rights to request hearings, Department disclosure of evidence within 30 days, hearing scheduling, and standards of proof (Department bears burden to show substantial evidence of noncompliance and aggravating circumstances). Decisions of the Secretary on debarment are final and not subject to further administrative review; judicial review is available under IAA section 204(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of suspension, cancellation, or debarment by the Secretary (§96.90)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on the (limited) administrative and judicial reviewability of Secretary adverse actions, exhaustion requirements for procedures in §§96.84/96.88/96.89, and availability of judicial review under 42 U.S.C. 14924(d) (IAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as provided in the listed procedural sections, adverse actions by the Secretary are not administratively reviewable; certain final actions (suspension, cancellation, debarment) are subject to judicial review and litigants may petition district courts per 5 U.S.C. 706.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of information to the public about accreditation and approval status (§96.92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accrediting entities must maintain and make available at least monthly: (1) name/address/contact for each accredited/approved agency/person; (2) names denied accreditation or approval not subsequently accredited; (3) names subject to suspension/cancellation/refusal to renew/debarment; (4) other information authorized for public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accrediting entities must also provide, upon request, confirmation of pending application status and brief statements of reasons for adverse actions, including identity and conduct of any foreign supervised providers when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of information about complaints against accredited agencies and approved persons (§96.93)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accrediting entities must maintain written records documenting each complaint and steps taken; they must confirm whether there have been substantiated complaints and have procedures for disclosing information about substantiated complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public disclosure must balance transparency with privacy and procedural fairness; accrediting entities must have disclosure procedures for substantiated complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports to the Secretary about accredited agencies and approved persons (§96.94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual and semi-annual reporting obligations to the Secretary, including semi-annual summaries covering accreditation/approval status, denials, adverse actions, substantiated complaints and their impacts, complaint-review metrics (shortest/longest/average/median review times), patterns in complaints, lists of disruption/dissolution/UCT/serious-harm cases by agency and country, and summaries of unsubstantiated or declined complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to these periodic reports, accrediting entities must immediately notify the Secretary when they learn an accredited agency/person ceased providing adoption services, transferred cases/records, withdrew a pending renewal application, when they accredit/approve, renew accreditation/approval, or take adverse action impacting status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accrediting entity record-retention requirement for accreditation decision-making (§96.7 and §96.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accrediting entities must retain all records relating to accreditation (and approval) decision-making for at least 10 years; the Secretary may require retention for a longer period but not shorten below 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This retention requirement supports oversight, reporting, and possible future review of accreditation/approval decisions; accrediting entities must keep accurate records of decision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation consideration of prior denials (§96.27(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating an application for accreditation or approval, accrediting entities must take into account reasons underlying a previous denial of accreditation or approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires reviewers to consider an applicant's past regulatory history and any corrective actions or persistent deficiencies that influenced prior denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of a home study recommendation practical steps (§96.47 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps and timelines for withdrawing a home-study recommendation that a family be found suitable to adopt abroad, including timelines to notify adoptive parents, primary providers, and USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule incorporates practical notification steps to ensure appropriate parties are informed promptly of a withdrawal decision affecting suitability determinations.
